children.label: d
children.prompt: Graph the relation $\max\{x+y,x-y\}=t$ on the Cartesian plane, where $t>0$.

inlines.text: Both expressions must be at most
, with at least one equal to

answer.worked:
$\max\{x+y,x-y\}=t$ means $x+y\leq t$ and $x-y\leq t$, with at least one equality.

When $x+y=t$, the line is $y=t-x$. The other inequality gives
$$\begin{align*}x-(t-x)&\leq t\\2x-t&\leq t\\2x&\leq2t\\x&\leq t.\end{align*}$$
This is the ray on $y=t-x$ extending upwards and left from $(t,0)$.

When $x-y=t$, the line is $y=x-t$. The other inequality gives
$$\begin{align*}x+(x-t)&\leq t\\2x-t&\leq t\\2x&\leq2t\\x&\leq t.\end{align*}$$
This is the ray on $y=x-t$ extending downwards and left from $(t,0)$.

The rays cross the y-axis at $(0,t)$ and $(0,-t)$. Include their common vertex because $\max\{t+0,t-0\}=t$. Since $x$ and $y$ are real, draw both rays continuously.

spec.mathematics: The branches are y=t-x for x≤t and y=x-t for x≤t, with t>0. The included vertex is (t,0); the y-intercepts are (0,t) and (0,-t). Drawing coordinates are X=x/t and Y=y/t, so the displayed vertex (1,0) represents (t,0). Equal positive scaling preserves both slopes and the graph topology.
